preregistration_contract: Written and committed BEFORE any sample was solved. Sample count, seeds, coefficient box, derived-coefficient map, quantities of interest, convergence gate and the surrogate designs below are the design of record; anything that had to change afterwards is recorded in `deviations` with its reason, and the seeds make the sample points themselves reproducible without trusting this file.

case.name: NASA TMR 2D zero-pressure-gradient flat plate, fine level
case.why_this_case: cheapest case the lab owns that has a trusted published reference: 80.9 s serial for the cold baseline, and its Cd sits +0.29% from the CFL3D SST-V value, so the coefficient band can be read against a real reference rather than only against itself

coefficients.name: a1
coefficients.note: increased only; the nominal IS the lower bound

kappa.note: its published interval [0.38, 0.42] is named in the docket item but kappa is not one of the five coefficients that item put in the box; held so the box stays the docketed one

held_fixed.mesh: held; no refinement in this study
held_fixed.numerics: held; fvSchemes, fvSolution and relaxation unchanged

derived_coefficient_map.gamma_i: beta_i/betaStar - sigma_wi kappa^2 / sqrt(betaStar) (Menter 1994 log-layer relation), recomputed for EVERY sample including the nominal one
derived_coefficient_map.why: OpenFOAM's kOmegaSST reads gamma1 and gamma2 as free coefficients. Moving betaStar or beta_i without recomputing gamma leaves the model off its own log layer, which is a different model, not a perturbed one. Enforcing the relation at the nominal point does not reproduce OpenFOAM's defaults (gamma1 0.553167 vs 5/9 = 0.555556, 0.43% apart; gamma2 0.440355 vs 0.44, 0.08% apart), so this study solves BOTH nominal points and reports the difference as a measured number instead of absorbing it into the band.

quantities_of_interest.name: cd
quantities_of_interest.definition: plate drag coefficient, Aref = 2, magUInf = 1, forceCoeffs on patch plate

quantities_of_interest.name: cf_station
quantities_of_interest.definition: skin friction at the TMR station x = 0.970084071

design.sampling: maximin Latin hypercube, best of 400 draws
design.marginals: uniform over each published interval. STATED ASSUMPTION: the intervals are epistemic, so the uniform is a sampling choice made to get a density the chaos and process fits need, not a claim about how the coefficients are distributed. The interval-valued reading of the result is the min/max envelope, which is reported alongside every probabilistic band and is the number the model channel may carry.
design.n_train_rationale: 21 terms in a total-order-2 polynomial chaos expansion over 5 variables, at the oversampling ratio of 2 the source paper uses for its point-collocation fits
design.joint_not_one_at_a_time: every sample moves all five coefficients at once; the motorbike stage of this docket item ran one-at-a-time corners and its own report states that band is a lower bound on the joint range

solve_protocol.restart: every sample restarts from the converged baseline field
solve_protocol.iterations_evidence: measured on a probe restart: Cd at 1500 iterations differs from Cd at 2000 by 3.5e-8 (0.0013% of Cd), against a band expected in the percent range
solve_protocol.gate_meaning: Cd peak-to-peak over the final 50 iterations; a sample that fails is reported as a failure, not quietly dropped
solve_protocol.concurrency: at most 5 native serial solves, reduced by the number of dafoam containers up

planned_analysis.monte_carlo: empirical band from the training samples: min/max envelope, mean, sigma, 5-95 percentile
planned_analysis.polynomial_chaos: non-intrusive point-collocation PCE on the Legendre basis (uniform germ), total order 1 and 2, least squares, leave-one-out scored; Sobol indices from the expansion coefficients
planned_analysis.surrogate: Gaussian process, anisotropic squared exponential plus nugget, hyperparameters by marginal likelihood, leave-one-out and held-out validation
planned_analysis.comparison: all three bands on the SAME sample set, plus the held-out set both surrogates are scored on

source_verification.how: The docket item recorded the intervals numerically but cited the paper only by title. Every interval below was read off the source's own Table 3 in the NASA NTRS copy of the conference version (ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/20160005982), which is the full text; the AIAA Journal version is paywalled and was NOT opened, so a number that changed between conference and journal would not have been caught.

provenance_per_interval.betaStar: Wilcox states tau_xy/k = 3/10 so betaStar = (tau_xy/k)^2 = 9/100; the interval comes from the source AUTHOR ASSUMING tau_xy/k in [0.28, 0.32]. It is an assumed range around a quoted value, not a measured one, and the docket item's phrase 'from Wilcox's measured stress ratio' overstates it. Wilcox, Turbulence Modeling for CFD, 3rd ed., 2006.
provenance_per_interval.a1: upper bound from Georgiadis and Yoder, NASA/TM-2013-217851: 'values of a1 greater than 0.40 were very similar to the unbounded BSL model. Therefore, the range of a1 investigated here was restricted to 0.31 <= a1 <= 0.40.' The increase-only rule is a PRIVATE COMMUNICATION from Menter to the first author, June 2014, quoted in the source: 'One can only increase a1 - decreasing it interferes with the log layer calibration.' Cite it as a private communication; there is no Menter publication behind it.
provenance_per_interval.sigma_w1: verified at [0.3, 0.7]. The source reuses its Wilcox-2006 intervals for coefficients the models share, but sigma_w's W2006 interval is [0.5, 0.7]; the SST table widens the lower bound to 0.3 and gives no reason.
provenance_per_interval.betaStar_over_beta1: from Wilcox's betaStar/beta0 = 1.25 +/- 0.06, set for W2006 (whose own standard value is 1.2712) and reused for SST. NOTE THE ASYMMETRY: SST's standard value 1.20 sits 0.01 above the interval's lower bound, so this coefficient is very nearly one-sided upward and beta1 can essentially only decrease.
provenance_per_interval.betaStar_over_beta2: numbers verified, RATIONALE NOT PUBLISHED. The source states no derivation for [1.05, 1.45]; the surrounding text says only that 'little more information is available regarding plausible domains for SST closure coefficients.' This study uses the interval as published and says here that it rests on nothing the reader can check.
provenance_per_interval.kappa: [0.38, 0.42] from Bailey, Vallikivi, Hultmark and Smits, JFM 749 (2014): kappa = 0.40 +/- 0.02 in turbulent pipe flow. The interval is centred on 0.40 while SST's standard value is 0.41, so the nominal is NOT the interval midpoint. Held at 0.41 here.

log_layer_relation.equations: gamma_i = beta_i/betaStar - sigma_wi kappa^2 / sqrt(betaStar), the source's Eqs. (26)-(27), identical to the NASA Turbulence Modeling Resource SST page and to Menter 1994.
log_layer_relation.does_the_source_enforce_it: INFERRED, NOT QUOTED. gamma1 and gamma2 are introduced as derived and do not appear among the nine coefficients Table 3 varies, and the source perturbs the RATIOS betaStar/beta_i rather than beta_i, which only makes sense if gamma is reconstructed. No sentence says so.
log_layer_relation.why_it_matters_in_openfoam: OpenFOAM's kOmegaSST exposes gamma1 and gamma2 as free coefficients with hard-coded defaults and has no kappa at all. Perturbing betaStar, beta_i or sigma_w without writing gamma yourself does not reproduce the source's design - it breaks log-layer consistency - and perturbing kappa does nothing whatever. This study writes gamma1 and gamma2 for every sample for that reason.

source_verification.method_design_confirmed_against_source: point-collocation non-intrusive polynomial chaos, Latin hypercube points, Legendre basis for bounded epistemic inputs, polynomial order 2 and oversampling ratio 2.0 - all four stated verbatim in the source's Section IV. This study's registered design matches all four.
source_verification.no_published_band_to_compare_against: The source does not run a flat plate; its cases are the axisymmetric transonic bump and RAE 2822. The study that does - Erb and Hosder, Computers & Fluids 227 (2021) 105027, SST coefficient UQ on the TMR 2D zero-pressure-gradient plate - is paywalled and was not opened, so its numbers are NOT in this record and this study's band is not claimed to agree or disagree with any published flat-plate band.
corrections_to_the_docket_entry: conference version is AIAA 2015-2461 (AIAA AVIATION, Dallas, June 2015), not AIAA 2015-0430
author order is Schaefer, West, Hosder, Rumsey, Carlson, Kleb - West is second, not third
the betaStar interval is assumed by the source's author around Wilcox's quoted ratio, not measured by Wilcox

Platteeuw, Loeven and Bijl (AIAA 2008-2150) is prior art for chaos applied to RANS coefficients but is not cited by this source and is not its method basis; the method citation is Hosder, Walters and Balch, AIAA Journal 48(12), 2010

box_is_a_subset.held_and_why: sigma_k1, sigma_k2 and sigma_w2 carry published intervals in the same table and are HELD at their standard values here, and kappa is held at 0.41. The docket item put five coefficients in the box and this study honours that box. The consequence is stated rather than left to be noticed: an envelope over 5 of the 9 published intervals is a LOWER BOUND on the envelope over all nine. Widening to nine is named as follow-up, not claimed here.

difference.meaning: the measured cost of OpenFOAM's rounded gamma1 = 5/9 against the log-layer-consistent 0.553167. It is reported because it is the size of the error a coefficient study makes when it perturbs betaStar and leaves gamma alone.

dominance_diagnostic.question: does the leading coefficient act directly, or through gamma1?
dominance_diagnostic.finding: sigma_w1 owns the band because sigma_w1 owns gamma1. gamma1 is not a free coefficient in this study -- it is reconstructed from the log-layer relation, in which sigma_w1 enters with the largest lever -- and Cd tracks gamma1 far more tightly than it tracks any coefficient sampled directly. THE CONSEQUENCE FOR COMPARISON: a coefficient study that leaves gamma at its default while moving sigma_w1 is moving only the omega-equation diffusion and will find sigma_w1 nearly inert. The motorbike stage of this docket item is such a study. The two studies' sigma_w1 rankings are therefore not the same quantity and must not be read against each other.

findings.band_dwarfs_the_validation_discrepancy: The case's own agreement with CFL3D is +0.29% on Cd. The joint coefficient band is 8.576e-04 wide, 30.3% of the reference value — about 104 times the discrepancy the validation is usually reported as. A validated case is not a case with a small model channel; it is a case whose closure happened to be calibrated near the answer.
findings.log_layer_correction_exceeds_the_validat: Simply making gamma1 consistent with the log-layer relation, at otherwise nominal coefficients, moves Cd by +0.433% — larger than the +0.29% gap to CFL3D that this case is validated on. The rounding of gamma1 to 5/9 in OpenFOAM's defaults is not a rounding as far as this QoI is concerned.
findings.dominant_coefficient: sigma_w1, total-effect variance share 0.925, with the other four sharing 0.075. See dominance_diagnostic: the effect runs through the derived gamma1.
findings.published_ranking_does_not_transfer: The source paper finds betaStar dominant for drag and skin friction in transonic wall-bounded flow. Here betaStar's total-effect share is 0.022 and its correlation with Cd is essentially zero. The ranking measured on this incompressible zero-pressure-gradient plate is not the published transonic one, which is what running it was for.
findings.the_process_surrogate_is_overconfident: Its held-out z-RMS is 2.91: on the ten solves it never saw, its errors are about three times the posterior standard deviation it claimed for them. Its MEAN is good (held-out Q2 0.9629) and its band agrees with the direct one, but its own error bars are not yet a trustworthy statement about a point it has not solved, and are not used as one anywhere in this record.
findings.the_three_propagations_agree: Chaos and process surrogate land within 7.6% of the direct standard deviation, on held-out data neither saw. On this response the cheap fits are not buying accuracy over direct sampling — they are buying the variance decomposition and the ability to interrogate the box without solving again.

commit_provenance.note: The results landed inside fa4191f5, whose message is about a different agent's literature review. That is not a mis-description by this study's author: two agents were committing on the same branch and the other one's `git add -A` swept this study's staged files into its commit before this study's own commit ran. Recorded here because a later audit reading `git log` for this work would otherwise find the wrong message attached to it, and every file it touched is listed in that commit's stat.
